articles.summary: Each month, Cyabra's experts share the articles, reports, and investigations shaping the conversation around misinformation, narrative intelligence and deepfakes. This September, from AI chatbots buckling under sustained misinformation pressure to the growing legal fight against deepfake harm, one thing is clear: as generative AI reshapes how false narratives are created and corrected, distinguishing reliable information from AI-amplified falsehoods is more critical than ever.
articles.title: Misinformation Monthly – November

articles.summary: Cyabra’s research on five competitive 2026 midterm races found that inauthentic activity on X peaked on Election Day, when fabricated Michigan and Ohio results drew 3.4 million views before polls closed.
articles.title: How Fake Results Outran the Count on Election Day

articles.summary: Based on a talk by Cyabra’s CEO Dan Brahmy at AMEC 2026, this article covers how inauthentic accounts amplify real complaints, what the Cracker Barrel and American Eagle backlashes reveal, and how to decide whether to respond based on which concerns are authentic and who is driving them.
articles.title: Ignore, Monitor, or Escalate: Deciding When a Backlash Deserves a Response

articles.summary: Real shoppers drove the Black Friday backlash against Target, Amazon and Walmart. But Cyabra's research found inauthentic accounts crowding the replies, especially under Amazon's own posts, and growing sharply into deal week.
articles.title: Inauthentic Accounts Amplified the Black Friday Backlash Against Target, Amazon and Walmart
